Answer from John: I’m Co-Founder of Rise25, which I co-founded in 2016 with Dr. Jeremy Weisz. 
Before that, I owned my own law firm in Silicon Valley representing startups and small businesses. I also started a digital publishing business, centered around my podcast.  I’ve also hosted and produced over 1,500 podcast episodes on Smart Business Revolution and other podcasts.
In its early years, Rise25 was focused on hosting small group mastermind events around the country, often in partnership with business conferences. 
Around 2018, we had many clients asking for help with launching podcasts so we pivoted to focusing 100% on building a podcast company.  
Earlier in my career, I worked as a Writer in Presidential Letters and Messages at the White House in the Clinton years and as a speechwriter for the Governor of California.  


 Answer from Jeremy Weisz: Co-Founder of Rise25, which I co-founded in 2016 with John Corcoran. Before that, I owned a chiropractic and massage facility in Chicago. I started the INspiredINsider podcast in 2008. Prior to that, I was also Senior Producer for the very early successful business podcast, Mixergy, and started working with them in 2008.

John: I’ve been heavily influenced by entrepreneurial peers in EO San Francisco and mentors like Michael Port, Jason Swenk and Charles McGlashan. I also read and have been influenced by many business books such as The E-Myth Revisited, Built to Sell, and Scaling Up. I’m also influenced by my family and my kids, and the desire to create a business that helps more people to build amazing relationships with clients and referral partners using podcasts.

Jeremy: I have many influences and certain books like "Never Split the Difference," "Shoe Dog," and "The Four Agreements" come to mind. I listen to 2-5 books per week on Audible.
Yes, I listen to them at 2.5 speed, so I get through them.
I'm also an EO. I'm in EO Chicago, and I have a great network there of peers. I'm always a part of different masterminds because I believe in collaborating and just learning from others. So I've been in the Titans Mastermind for 7 years with Brian Kurtz. And other masterminds as well.
In addition, family is important. My dad has been an influence, and my grandfather has been a big influence. He was a Holocaust survivor, and I saw what he went through. That gives me a lot of my perspective on persistence and what persistence and survival really is.
column8:
John:  My kids. I have 4 kids between the ages of 15 and 6. They challenge and inspire me every day. I am proud to have been married to my wife for 20+ years. I am proud to have used a podcast to transition away from unhappily practicing law to a life of entrepreneurship which I have found fulfilling and interesting.  I am also proud to have built Rise25 into a seven-figure, fully remote agency that supports ~40 team members worldwide. I am proud of all of the clients who we have taught how to create a ROI-producing podcast and who have built amazing relationships with clients and referral partners through their podcasts. 

During law school, while I was working at a large corporate law firm, I rallied my classmates to donate a day of their summer salary to a public interest program to help pay expenses for other law students working in the public interest over the summer. 

Jeremy: My greatest life achievement is a tough one. I'll say there are a few categories. 
From the family one, parenting kids with my wife and trying to instill great values with them. 
From a health perspective, just staying on track with health goals is important because that allows me to stay healthy and work hard and have lots of energy. After I tore my meniscus a year ago, I started swimming and now I wake up really early in the morning and I swim about five miles a week and get up before everyone else is awake.
From a sports perspective... I played a lot of competitive travel baseball growing up and that really fueled my competitive nature and fueled my work ethic from an early age. We played 60+ games in a summer and I was a catcher and caught almost every game.  
From a business perspective, as John expressed - I am also proud to have built Rise25 into a seven-figure, fully remote agency that supports ~40 team members worldwide.

Our most successful marketing campaigns have been utilizing our own podcasts. We feature clients, prospective clients, referral partners and strategic partners, and we use our podcasts to get introductions from clients to others who fit our ICP. We also use our podcasts to do cold outreach to individuals who look like great prospects, especially inside of shared interest business communities we belong to (i.e. EO, Digital Agency Elite mastermind, Provisors, etc.). 

We also strategically invite our clients onto our own podcasts to educate our current clients about best practices they can utilize, to deepen relationships with current clients, to generate more referrals, and to explore other services we can deliver to those clients.  
Also effective for us has been doing in-person and virtual presentations (webinars) for various audiences, and it is something we would like to do more of. We have done 700+ webinars over the past 10+ years. 

Another effective strategy has been building up our email list and doing email marketing. We had around 75K email subscribers at our peak and we could refocus our energies back towards building up that channel again. 

We have also done cold email outreach and utilized an article strategy for outreach, where we feature cold prospects in articles which we publish. 

We also have a book (tentatively titled Predictable Podcast Profits) which is fully written and ready to be released. We have been waiting for the right time to release it.   

Of course, each of these projects require time and attention, and we would love to be able to  focus more attention on them in the future.

One of the big benefits of working for us is we allow our team to do meaningful work on a flexible schedule, fully remote. Many of our team members have family members they need to care for and really prize the flexibility. Probably half of our team is working mothers who work hard and deeply appreciate the opportunity to be able to be part of a collaborative team and they can work around childcare responsibilities. 

We have a 'no assholes' policy so we will not tolerate working with anyone (either employees or clients) who we don't like working with. 

At the moment, our entire team is comprised of contractors, and we do not provide traditional benefits. We have had employees in the past. 

The only person who has health care benefits at the moment is Jeremy, and that was added only a few years ago. However, we have found for certain offshore staff, there are other benefits which we can provide which has yielded great loyalty and appreciation. So for particular team members, we guarantee them a certain amount of hours and a flat amount of pay which they can rely on. We also have certain team members who we provide a stipend to cover their home internet and/or their cell phone bill, and we have found this has led to great loyalty and appreciation. 

We also provide annual end of year (December) bonuses based on company performance, and access to additional online training.

We follow the EOS and Scaling Up meeting models. We have a “Weekly meeting” twice per week - at the beginning and the end of the week - where we review all of the onboarding clients and key KPIs. Through this meeting, we keep tabs on all of the clients and their onboarding process, and the goal is to anticipate and surface any issues before they become big problems. 

We have a weekly KPI meeting which is more oriented towards reviewing KPIs like speed to reply to customer support tickets, time to write show notes, total hours and average hours worked by department,  and marketing KPIs. We have a Level 10 meeting where we review larger ongoing issues and monitor our company rocks.
Each team (i.e. PM team, content marketing team, developers) has a short daily standup meetings. There are other regular meetings as well but those are the core meetings.
